title: Feature: agent office, part 2: make the agents move
body:
### What it should do
The agent office scene (admin console → Agents) now has a real venue and six people, but they stand still. Bring it to life: each agent does its own job when it is **working**, waves when **finished**, and stays put holding its red flag when it **needs a look**.

- **Test customer** (`.r-tester`): walks a loop between the two game tables, phone in hand.
- **Technical agent** (`.r-tech`): stays behind the front desk, typing (arms bobbing). Never leaves the desk: the desk hides its legs.
- **Builder** (`.r-builder`): walks back and forth on the stage and hammers (the front arm holds the hammer).
- **Reviewer** (`.r-reviewer`): patrols the floor between the tables, clipboard up.
- **Pull request checks** (`.r-checks`): paces side to side in front of the entrance.
- **Backup** (`.r-backup`): carries its box from the bar area to the storage room door and back.
- **Finished** (`.done`): a gentle, slow wave with the front arm (it is raised already; swing it about 20 degrees).
- **String lights** (`.agbulb` with `.b0`, `.b1`, `.b2`): a slow twinkle, a little brighter at night (`.agscene.night`).

### Who uses it
Roy and staff

### Where in the app
Admin console → Agents tab (`agentsBody` in js/18-support-staff.js; styles under "the agent office" in css/games.css)

### Done when
- [ ] Each working agent moves at its own spot and faces the way it walks
- [ ] Finished agents wave; agents that need a look stand still with their flag
- [ ] Nobody walks through a desk, the bar or off the stage, and speech bubbles move with their agent
- [ ] With the phone's "reduce motion" setting on, nothing moves (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`)
- [ ] Smooth on a phone: animate only `transform` and `left`/`top`, no JavaScript timers
- [ ] Works on a phone-sized screen
- [ ] The check in agents/regressions.json for the agent office still passes
- [ ] `bash agents/check_all.sh` passes

### Notes for the builder (how the scene is built: read before starting)
- Claude built part 1 by hand in a coding session (commit "Agent office: a real venue scene"). Follow its pattern; don't rebuild the scene.
- The scene is a 400 by 500 box. Every agent is an `<a class="agw r-NAME STATE">` placed with `left`/`top` in percent (its feet), and `transform: translate(-50%,-100%)` keeps the feet on that spot. Their resting spots are in `AG_HOME`. STATE is `work`, `done`, `fail` or `idle`.
- Paths: give each working agent a `@keyframes` that changes `left` and `top` in percent, like `.agw.work.r-tester{animation:agp-tester 16s linear infinite}`. Keep the speech bubble inside the `.agw` so it follows.
- Facing: animate `.agfig` with `scaleX(-1)` while walking left (a second keyframes with `step-end` timing at the same moments).
- Each person's parts (inside `agPerson`): `.agbod` (whole body, good for a small bob), `.agleg-l`, `.agleg-r` (swing them in turn for walking), `.agarm` (front arm: hammer, phone, clipboard, wave), `.agarm-b` (back arm), `.agcarry` (backup's box), `.agflag`. Their pivot points are already set in the CSS (`transform-origin` with `transform-box: view-box`): rotate them, don't move them.
- Layers: the background SVG (`.agbg`), then the agents (`z-index: 4`, the technical agent `2` so the front desk covers its legs), then the foreground SVG (`.agfg`: bar, front desk, Icee's desk, `z-index: 3`).
- Use the existing colors only: navy #16255a, orange #f6892f, green #2f8a4c.
- Don't change how status is worked out (`agState`, `agNews`, `agLatestRun`): that part is done and tested.

_Split between Claude and the builder on Nov 3, 2026, so the builder works from a clear pattern. Start the builder by adding the `claude` label._
